Corollary
[Regular Level Set Theorem] ↗ prop:slice-chart-euclidean 1. chA:A.26

Let $\bar{M}$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, and let $\Phi : \bar{M} \to N$ be a smooth map. Every regular level set of $\Phi $ is a properly embedded submanifold of $M$ whose codimension is equal to $\dim N$.

The local model is Proposition 4: at each regular point, the slice chart of $\Phi $ read in charts of $\bar{M}$ and $N$ exhibits the level set as an affine slice of dimension $\dim \bar{M} - \dim N$. What remains is the global step: assembling these charts into a smooth atlas on $\Phi ^{-1}(c)$, with smooth transition maps on the overlaps, and identifying its topology with the subspace topology, which is what makes the embedding proper. That step is carried out below in the codimension-one case $N = \mathbb {R}$; the general case remains open.

Every application of this corollary in the present development takes $N = \mathbb {R}$, so the codimension-one case suffices throughout and nothing below depends on the general statement.
